top_temples.name: Mankameshwar Temple, Agra
top_temples.location_note: Old part of Agra city; believed over 5,000 years old and associated with the Pandavas, the oldest Shiva temple in Agra.

top_temples.name: Balkeshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Yamuna in Agra; a roughly 700-year-old riverside shrine, especially popular during Sawan.

top_temples.name: Shri Khatu Shyam Ji Temple, Agra
top_temples.location_note: Opened 2023; the largest Khatu Shyam Ji temple in Uttar Pradesh.

top_temples.name: Dayalbagh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Agra; one of the largest Radha Soami temples, known for its architecture.

top_temples.name: Kailash Temple, Agra
top_temples.location_note: Agra; roughly 5,000-year-old temple noted for its Shivlings said to originate from Mount Kailash.

top_temples.name: Bade Hanuman Ji Mandir (Lete Hanuman Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Prayagraj (Allahabad); features a rare 20-ft reclining Hanuman idol below ground level, the city's most famous temple.

top_temples.name: Alopi Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Prayagraj; a Shakti Peetha with no idol, worship centers on a wooden doli on a marble platform.

top_temples.name: Patalpuri Temple
top_temples.deity: Various deities, with the sacred Akshayavat tree
top_temples.location_note: Within Allahabad Fort; an underground temple housing the immortal Akshayavat banyan tree.

top_temples.name: Nagvasuki Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Ganges in Prayagraj; a prominent temple to the serpent god.

top_temples.name: Mankameshwar Mandir, Allahabad
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Yamuna near Saraswati Ghat, Prayagraj.

top_temples.name: Ram Janmabhoomi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ayodhya's central and most significant shrine, believed to be Rama's birthplace; a three-story temple with five mandaps.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Garhi
top_temples.location_note: A fort-like hilltop shrine in Ayodhya reached via 76 steps, traditionally regarded as the protector of the city.

top_temples.name: Shree Baba Alakhnath Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of four Shiva temples marking the corners of Bareilly city.

top_temples.name: Shri Baba Dhopeshwar Nath Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Cantonment area of Bareilly; a distinctive water temple.

top_temples.name: Shri Trivati Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bareilly; originally constructed around 1474, another of the city's four corner Shiva temples.

top_temples.name: Bada Bagh Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bareilly; one of the city's most prominent Hanuman shrines.

top_temples.name: Shri Baba Pashupati Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bareilly; a revered ancient temple.

top_temples.name: Kamadgiri Temple
top_temples.location_note: Chitrakoot's central shrine, on the Kamadgiri hill; pilgrims perform a circumambulation (parikrama) of the hill, principal deity of Chitrakoot Dham.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Dhara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Kamadgiri hill in Chitrakoot; a natural spring shrine associated with Hanuman, distinct from the Bharat Milap temple used for the MP-side Chitrakoot entry.

top_temples.name: Dudheshwar Nath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Ghaziabad; said to be thousands of years old, one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Raj Nagar
top_temples.location_note: Raj Nagar, Ghaziabad; a major spiritual and cultural center, especially busy during Janmashtami.

top_temples.name: Chopla Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Ghaziabad; one of the city's older Hanuman temples.

top_temples.name: Durga Temple, Ghaziabad
top_temples.deity: Durga, with Shiv Parivar, Ganesh, and Shani
top_temples.location_note: Ghaziabad city.

top_temples.name: Manan Dham
top_temples.location_note: On the main Meerut highway in Ghaziabad; a well-crafted Shiva shrine.

top_temples.name: J.K. Temple (Radhakrishna Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Sarvodaya Nagar, Kanpur; built in white marble, one of Kanpur's most visited temples.

top_temples.name: Anandeshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kanpur; built in the 18th century.

top_temples.name: Bhitargaon Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bhitargaon, about 35 km from Kanpur; the largest surviving brick temple from the Gupta Empire, late 5th century.

top_temples.name: Jain Glass Temple, Kanpur
top_temples.location_note: Kanpur; known for hand-crafted glass murals and statues.

top_temples.name: Panki Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On the outskirts of Kanpur, near Panki Railway Station.

top_temples.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Lucknow
top_temples.location_note: Lucknow; a marble replica of the Varanasi Kashi Vishwanath Temple.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Setu Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Lucknow; a major pilgrimage site especially on Tuesdays and Saturdays, features a large black-stone Hanuman sculpture.

top_temples.name: Mankameshwar Temple, Lucknow
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Lucknow city; believed to be among its oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Chandrika Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bakshi Ka Talab area, Lucknow; established roughly 300 years ago.

top_temples.name: Rangaji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Lucknow; built 1851, blends Italian colonnade, Rajput-style gate, and South Indian gopuram architecture.

top_temples.name: Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mathura's most significant shrine, marking Krishna's traditional birthplace.

top_temples.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mathura; dating to 1814, features a black marble idol.

top_temples.name: Gita Mandir (Birla Mandir), Mathura
top_temples.location_note: About 6.5 km from Mathura Junction; walls inscribed with all 700 verses of the Bhagavad Gita.

top_temples.name: Kesava Deo Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near the main Krishna Janmabhoomi complex in Mathura.

top_temples.name: Bhuteshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 500 m from Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura; one of the 108 significant Shiva temples in India.

top_temples.name: Augharnath Temple (Kali Paltan Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Meerut's oldest and most frequented Shiva temple; the Shiva linga is believed to be swayambhu (self-manifested).

top_temples.name: Digambar Jain Temple, Meerut
top_temples.location_note: One of Meerut's oldest temples, featuring seven ornate altar spires.

top_temples.name: Mansa Devi Temple, Meerut
top_temples.location_note: Meerut; played a role in the 1857 freedom struggle, hosts a major annual fair.

top_temples.name: Surajkund Temple (Baba Manohar Lal Mahadev Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: One of Meerut's oldest temples, located alongside the Shahpir Mausoleum.

top_temples.name: Lakshmi Narayan Mandir, Modi Nagar
top_temples.location_note: Modi Nagar area of Meerut; spread over more than 15 acres.

top_temples.name: Lalita Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Naimisharanya's central shrine; a Shakti Peetha where the heart of Sati is believed to have fallen.

top_temples.name: Chakratirtha
top_temples.deity: Sacred tirtha associated with Brahma and Vishnu
top_temples.location_note: A short walk from Lalita Devi Temple in Naimisharanya; the mythological site where Brahma's discus (chakra) formed a holy water body.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Sector 33
top_temples.location_note: Sector 33, Noida; a seven-storied temple with gold murals, especially busy on Janmashtami.

top_temples.name: Shree Jagannath Temple, Sector 34
top_temples.location_note: Sector 34, Noida; opened 2006, hosts an annual Rath Yatra.

top_temples.name: Ayyappa Temple, Sector 62
top_temples.location_note: Sector 62, Noida; popular among South Indian residents, regarded as a protector of the city.

top_temples.name: Noida Kalibari Temple, Sector 26
top_temples.location_note: Sector 26, Noida; established 1984, an important center for the Bengali community.

top_temples.name: Sai Mandir, Noida
top_temples.location_note: Noida; built in white marble, maintained by Shri Sai Samiti.

top_temples.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Varanasi's defining shrine; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, known as the 'Golden Temple' for its gold-plated dome.

top_temples.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: Varanasi; established by the poet-saint Tulsidas.

top_temples.name: Durga Temple (Monkey Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Varanasi; noted for its red-stone architecture.

top_temples.name: Tulsi Manas Temple
top_temples.location_note: Varanasi; built 1964, named for saint-poet Tulsidas, walls inscribed with verses from the Ramcharitmanas.

top_temples.name: Annapurna Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Varanasi, near Kashi Vishwanath; associated with food and nourishment, known for community food offerings.

top_temples.name: Maa Vindhyavasini Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a hilltop overlooking the Ganga in Vindhyachal; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, the town's central shrine.

top_temples.name: Ashtabhuja Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a hillock about 8 km from Vindhyavasini Temple in Vindhyachal; part of the Trikon Parikrama circuit with the main temple.

top_temples.name: Banke Bihari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Vrindavan's most famous shrine; built in 1864, one of the holiest Krishna temples in India.

top_temples.name: Radha Raman Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest and most sacred temples in Vrindavan, distinct from Banke Bihari.
